key_insight: In this registry-based cohort of cancer patients in Northwest Russia, receiving at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose before the landmark date was associated with substantially better overall survival.
clinical_relevance: The study suggests COVID-19 vaccination may be an important survival-related protective factor for cancer patients, while AI-read chest CT findings also helped identify higher-risk patients.
method: Population-based retrospective cohort of 1,144 cancer patients linked across cancer registry, vaccination records, and AI-analyzed chest CT scans.
Used a landmark design to reduce immortal time bias, with primary analysis restricted to patients alive on March 1, 2021 (N=1,136).
Compared vaccinated vs unvaccinated survival with Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for clinical and imaging factors.
evidence_signal: Vaccination was uncommon (6.6%, 76/1,144) and was associated with higher 3-year overall survival (80.3% vs 45.7%) and lower adjusted mortality hazard (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25-0.64).
watch_item: Because this is an observational study, vaccinated patients may have differed from unvaccinated patients in ways that also affect survival, so causality cannot be confirmed.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
